findings.claim: ByID now goes through mapAll/kinOf. For any memory without an import_map row, kinOf calls Store.ImportedObservations, which reads every imported memory of the project, body included, and hashes each observation. The base ran one MappedTwins query keyed by content hash. A single-memory lookup therefore costs time and memory proportional to the size of the project's import history. It repeats on every ByID call for a hand-written memory, because nothing is cached.
proof_refs: observations.go:36-52 full-project import_map join that loads bodies

findings.claim: The hash of a single part is no longer a hash an observation answers to when it has several parts. A hand mirror that holds the text of one part (for example, a memory copied from just that part) matched through the stored content_hash in the base and is now missed. The rebuilt text also depends on every part's memory still existing. If a sibling part's memory is gone, the remaining part keeps its ' (part i/n)' title because the len(ps)>1 check fails, so it never matches its original text.
proof_refs: observations.go:78-80 the title suffix is stripped only when len(ps) > 1
observations.go:82-86 only whole-text hashes are emitted
